findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not match any method signature
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with zero arguments, but the only method with that name is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` defined in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm. There is no no-arg overload defined anywhere in the class hierarchy shown in this PR. This will not compile ("cannot find symbol"), breaking the build. The call should almost certainly be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() inverts the condition that gates filling WebAuthn form attributes, breaking passkeys on fresh (non-reauth) logins
findings.body: The new helper `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` requires `user != null` to return true. It replaces the previous explicit check `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` in both `authenticate()` (line ~115) and `challenge(context, error, field)` (line ~137), which used to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` precisely when there was NO pre-selected user (the normal, first-time login/conditional-UI discovery flow). With the new helper requiring `user != null`, `fillContextForm` is now only invoked when a user is already set (i.e., during re-authentication), and it is never invoked for the standard first-time login case where `context.getUser()` is null. This removes the WebAuthn challenge/RP-id/conditional-UI attributes from the rendered login form for all normal (non-reauthentication) logins, which would break the passwordless/passkeys discoverable-credential login flow entirely for the common case and contradicts existing tests (e.g. webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey, passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey) that expect the webauthn form to be present on a fresh login page where no user has yet been identified.

findings.title: Unused import left after replacing assertThrows(NoSuchElementException) assertions
findings.body: The import `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` is retained even though both usages of `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` were replaced by `MatcherAssert.assertThat(..., notNullValue())` assertions (lines ~200 and ~211 area in the diff). The import is now dead code; depending on the project's checkstyle configuration this may fail the build or is at least confusing dead code that should be removed.
